genre_claims_used.claim: ẹ̀sà is also known as Ìwí Egúngún and is associated with Egúngún ancestral veneration; devotees chant praises in ẹ̀sà mode
text content and performer identity do not reliably identify a genre; the same text can be used in several genres; vocal expression distinguishes them
ìjálá has vibrato; ẹ̀sà has no vibrato but vowel insertion and lengthening; a triply long [ooo] at the end of the first line recurs in ẹ̀sà
in the experiment [ooo] was inserted at the beginning of the first word of line 1; ẹ̀sà F0 was higher than ìjálá; ẹ̀sà was never vocalised with vibrato
one participant; pilot study; the poem is original, chosen to control content and familiarity

why_this_is_a_valid_labelled_equivalent: It is not offered as an inherited chant. It teaches the identifying features of ẹ̀sà/iwì delivery that the scholarship says distinguish the genre, and a short oríkì read closely. It does not supply an inherited iwì text and does not close the objective.

draft_lesson.title: iwì egúngún (ẹ̀sà): a modern oríkì and the marks of ẹ̀sà delivery
